First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 \\ 4 & 8\end{aligned}]
$$

 Notice that we can write the constraint equation as follows:

 

$$
\frac{{x}_{1}^{2}}{{2}^{2}}+\frac{{x}_{2}^{2}}{{1}^{2}}=1
$$

 This is an ellipse with semiaxes $a=2$ (along the ${x}_{1}$-axis) and $b=1$ (along the ${x}_{2}$-axis). If we introduce new variables

$\,$ ${y}_{1}=\frac{{x}_{1}}{2}\,$ and $\,{y}_{2}={x}_{2},$

 the equation of the ellipse will transform into ${y}_{1}^{2}+{y}_{2}^{2}=1$ or $‖y‖=1.$

 So, introducing a change-of-coordinate matrix 

 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}],
$$

 

 we obtain that $x=Py.$ Substituting this into the expression of the quadratic form, we get

 

$$
Q(x)={x}^{T}\,Ax=(Py)^{T}A\,(Py)={y}^{T}\,({P}^{T}AP)y={Q}^{′}(y).
$$

 As a result, since ${P}^{T}=P,$ the matrix of our quadratic form in new coordinates is 

 

$$
\begin{aligned}B & ={P}^{T}\,AP \\  & =PAP \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 \\ 4 & 8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 8 \\ 4 & 8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 8 \\ 8 & 8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

 Now, we maximize ${Q}^{′}(y)$ when $||y||=1,$ as usual.

 Since we are told that the maximum value of the quadratic form is $12,$ we have

 

$$
max{{Q}^{′}(y)\,|\,‖y‖=1}={\lambda }_{max}=12.
$$

 Next, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{max}}=12:$

 

$$
\begin{aligned}B-12I & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 8 \\ 8 & 8\end{aligned}]-12[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-16 & 8 \\ 8 & -4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 Seeking a non-zero solution of $(B-12I)y=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ Dividing $v$ by its norm $‖v‖=\sqrt{5},$ we get 

 

$$
{u}_{\text{max}}=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

 

 Finally, we map this vector back to the initial coordinate  system using the change-of-coordinates matrix:

 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{\text{max}} & =P{u}_{\text{max}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
